books.name: Ancyra
books.line: Today's Ankara, the chief city of the old Celtic land of Galatia and of the Roman province. On the north Galatian view, Paul wrote to churches in this region, which Acts mentions only in passing (Acts 16:6; 18:23).

books.name: Antioch in Syria
books.line: The church here, where the disciples were first called Christians (11:26), sends out Barnabas and Saul (13:1-3). Paul comes back here after his first two trips (14:26; 18:22).

books.name: Antioch in Syria
books.line: The great city where believers were first called Christians, and where Jewish and Gentile believers ate together. Here Paul opposed Peter to his face (2:11-14).

books.name: Ashdod
books.line: A Philistine city. The captured ark was set in the temple of Dagon here, and Dagon fell on his face before it (5:1-5). Acts calls the city Azotus (Acts 8:40).

books.name: Ashdod
books.line: The old Philistine city on the coast. Its people joined the plot against the wall (4:7), and some men of Judah married women from there (13:23-24).

books.name: Asia
books.line: The Roman province of the west coast, with Ephesus its great city, where Paul had worked (Acts 19). Placed roughly.

books.name: Athens
books.line: Paul speaks before the Areopagus about an altar to an unknown god (17:22-23). A few believe, among them Dionysius and a woman named Damaris (17:34).

books.name: Athens
books.line: Where Paul was willing to be left alone, so that he could send Timothy back to the Thessalonians (3:1-2).

books.name: Azotus
books.line: The old Philistine city of Ashdod, near the coast. Philip appears here after baptizing the Ethiopian official on the road to Gaza (8:26-40).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: Abraham digs a well and swears an oath with Abimelech here (21:22-33). Isaac lives here, and Jacob sets out from here for Haran (28:10).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: Samuel's sons served as judges here and took bribes (8:1-3). ‘From Dan to Beersheba’ named the whole land, north to south (3:20).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: ‘From Dan to Beersheba’ named the whole land, north to south (3:10; 24:2).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: ‘From Dan to Beersheba’ named the whole land (4:25). Elijah fled past it into the wilderness (19:3).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: The southern edge of Judah. Joash's mother came from here (12:1), and Josiah defiled the high places ‘from Geba to Beersheba’ (23:8).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: A town of Simeon (4:28). David's census ran ‘from Beersheba to Dan’ (21:2).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: Judah's southern edge. Jehoshaphat went out ‘from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim’ (19:4), and Hezekiah's Passover invitation ran ‘from Beersheba to Dan’ (30:5).

books.name: Beersheba
books.line: The people of Judah ‘settled from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom’ (11:30).

books.name: Berea
books.line: The Jews here receive the message eagerly and search the Scriptures every day to see if it is true (17:10-12).

books.name: Bethany
books.line: A village on the Mount of Olives where Jesus stays in his last week and is anointed with perfume (26:6-13).

books.name: Bethany
books.line: A village on the Mount of Olives, where Jesus stays in his last week and is anointed (14:3).

books.name: Bethany
books.line: A village on the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem. From near here Jesus blesses his disciples and is carried up into heaven (24:50-51).

books.name: Bethany
books.line: The village of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, ‘a little less than two miles’ from Jerusalem (11:18). Here Lazarus is raised and Jesus anointed.

books.name: Bethany beyond the Jordan
books.line: Where John baptized (1:28). One site east of the river is marked as the place, but its identification is not certain, and other places have been proposed.

books.name: Bethel
books.line: Abraham pitches his tent near here. Jacob dreams of a stairway to heaven and names the place Bethel, ‘house of God’ (28:10-22).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: Ai, where Israel was beaten and then won, lay ‘to the east of Bethel’ (7:2). Where Ai itself stood is debated.

books.name: Bethel
books.line: Deborah judged Israel between Ramah and Bethel (4:5). In the war with Benjamin the tribes went up to Bethel to ask God (20:18).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: One of the towns on Samuel's yearly circuit as judge, with Gilgal and Mizpah (7:16). Saul kept two thousand men at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel (13:2).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: Jeroboam set up one of his golden calves here (12:29), and a man of God from Judah cried out against its altar (13:1-2).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: Elijah and Elisha passed through it (2:2-3), youths jeered at Elisha on the road up (2:23), and Josiah tore down its altar (23:15).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: A town of the north, one of the cities Abijah took from Jeroboam (13:19).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: ‘The men of Bethel and Ai’ came home, 223 of them (2:28).

books.name: Bethel
books.line: Its men are on the list of the first return (7:32), and Benjamin's people lived there in Nehemiah's day (11:31).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin and is buried ‘on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)’ (35:19).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: Home of the young Levite who became Micah's priest (17:7) and of the Levite's concubine (19:1).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: The house of bread, where a famine began the story, and where Ruth gleaned, married Boaz and bore Obed (1:1; 1:19; 4:11).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: Jesse's town, where Samuel anointed David, the youngest son (16:1-13). David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep here (17:15).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: David's hometown. Asahel was buried here (2:32), and three of David's mighty men brought him water from its well (23:15-16).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: David's hometown. Three of his mighty men broke through the Philistines to bring him water from its well (11:15-19).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: David's town. Its men are counted among the first to come home, 123 of them (2:21).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: ‘The men of Bethlehem and Netophah’ are on the list of those who first came home (7:26).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: David's town, where Jesus is born and the Magi find him. From here the family flees to Egypt, off this map to the south-west (2:13-15).

books.name: Bethlehem
books.line: David's town, a few miles south of Jerusalem. Jesus is born here and laid in a manger; shepherds come from the fields nearby (2:4-20).

books.name: Bethsaida
books.line: A lakeside town where many mighty works were done, yet Jesus grieves that it did not turn back to God (11:21).

books.name: Bethsaida
books.line: A town at the north end of the lake. A blind man is healed here in two stages (8:22-26).

books.name: Bethsaida
books.line: The home town of Philip, Andrew and Peter (1:44), near where the Jordan runs into the lake. Its exact site is disputed.

books.name: Bithynia
books.line: A province on the coast south of the Black Sea. The Spirit kept Paul from entering it (Acts 16:7). Around AD 110 its governor, Pliny, wrote to the emperor about Christians there. Placed roughly.

books.name: Caesarea
books.line:
A port city Herod the Great built on the coast, where the Roman governors lived. Cornelius, a Roman officer, lives here (10:1), and Herod Agrippa dies here (12:23).

The governors' city on the coast. Paul is held here two years and speaks before Felix, Festus and King Agrippa (chapters 24 to 26).

books.name: Caesarea
books.line: Where Paul was held for two years before he was sent to Rome (Acts 23 to 26). Some think he wrote the letter here, as ‘an ambassador in chains’ (6:20).

books.name: Caesarea
books.line: Where Paul was held two years in Herod's palace (Acts 23:35). Some think he wrote the letter here.

books.name: Caesarea
books.line: Where Paul was held two years (Acts 23 to 26). A few think he wrote the letter here.

books.name: Caesarea
books.line: Where Paul was held two years (Acts 23 to 26). A few think he wrote the letter here.

books.name: Caesarea Philippi
books.line: Near a pagan shrine in the far north, Peter says, ‘You are the Christ’, and Jesus speaks of building his church (16:13-20).

books.name: Caesarea Philippi
books.line: A town at the foot of Mount Hermon. Near here Peter says, “You are the Christ” (8:27-30).

books.name: Cana
books.line: Where water became wine, the first sign (2:1-11). Two sites claim it, Kafr Kanna and Khirbet Qana, a few miles apart; so it is placed roughly.

books.name: Canaan
books.line: The land God promises to Abraham and his children (12:5-7; 17:8). The second map below shows it close up.

books.name: Canaan
books.line: The land God promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, ‘a land flowing with milk and honey’ (3:8; 6:4). Israel does not reach it in Exodus. Drawn roughly.

books.name: Canaan
books.line: The land ahead: ‘the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you’ (18:3). Many laws in the book look forward to life there. Drawn roughly.

books.name: Capernaum
books.line: A fishing town by the lake that becomes Jesus' home base (4:13), called ‘His own town’ (9:1). A Roman officer's servant is healed here (8:5-13).

books.name: Capernaum
books.line: A fishing town on the lake and Jesus' base in Galilee. Mark calls it his home (2:1).

books.name: Capernaum
books.line: A fishing town on the north shore of the lake. Jesus teaches in its synagogue, and heals a centurion's servant here (7:1-10).

books.name: Capernaum
books.line: A fishing town on the lake. Jesus stays here with his family and disciples; a royal official's son lies sick here, and Jesus teaches in its synagogue (6:59).

books.name: Cappadocia
books.line: A province of the high inland plateau. People from Cappadocia heard Peter at Pentecost (Acts 2:9). Placed roughly.

books.name: Colossae
books.line: A small town in the Lycus valley, where Epaphras planted the church (1:7). Paul had never been there (2:1).

books.name: Colossae
books.line: Philemon's town, as Colossians shows, where the church met in his house (verse 2; Colossians 4:9, 17).

books.name: Corinth
books.line: Paul stays a year and a half here, working with Aquila and Priscilla as a tentmaker (18:1-11). He is brought before Gallio, the governor of Achaia (18:12).

books.name: Corinth
books.line: Where Paul most likely wrote the letter, in the house of Gaius (16:23). Phoebe served the church at Cenchrea, Corinth's eastern port (16:1).

books.name: Corinth
books.line: Where the letter went: a Roman colony on the narrow neck of land in southern Greece, where Paul had started the church (1:2). Chloe's people brought him news of it (1:11).

books.name: Corinth
books.line: Where the letter went: “the church of God in Corinth” (1:1), the chief city of Achaia, where Paul had started the church and had made a painful second visit.

books.name: Corinth
books.line: Where Timothy brought Paul good news, and where Paul most likely wrote this letter (3:6; Acts 18:5).

books.name: Corinth
books.line: If Paul wrote the letter, he wrote it here, with Silvanus and Timothy, not long after the first (1:1; Acts 18:5).

books.name: Corinth
books.line: Where Erastus stayed behind (4:20).

books.name: Crete (Fair Havens)
books.line: A bay on the south coast of Crete where Paul's ship shelters. He warns against sailing on, but the ship leaves and is caught in a storm (27:8-20).

books.name: Crete
books.line: The island where Paul left Titus to appoint elders in every town (1:5). The mark is Fair Havens on its south coast, where Paul's ship once sheltered (Acts 27:8).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: David defeated the Arameans of Damascus and put garrisons among them (8:5-6).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: Rezon made himself king here (11:23-24). Asa paid its king to attack Israel (15:18-20), and Elijah was sent to the desert of Damascus (19:15).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: Capital of Aram, Naaman's home (5:12). Elisha went there and wept before Hazael (8:7-15), and Assyria took it (16:9).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: David defeated the Arameans of Damascus and put garrisons among them (18:5-6).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: The Aramean capital. Asa bought its king's help with the temple's silver (16:2), and its armies later struck Judah (24:23; 28:5).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: An old city in Syria. Saul asks for letters to its synagogues (9:2), meets the risen Jesus on the road to it, and is baptized there.

books.name: Damascus
books.line: Where, years before, the governor under King Aretas tried to arrest Paul, and he was let down in a basket through a window in the wall (11:32-33).

books.name: Damascus
books.line: Near here Paul met the risen Christ. After a time in Arabia he “later returned to Damascus” (1:17).

books.name: The Decapolis
books.line: ‘Ten cities’, a league of Greek towns mostly east of the Jordan. Crowds come from here to hear Jesus (4:25).

books.name: The Decapolis
books.line: ‘Ten Cities’ in Greek: a league of Greek-speaking towns, mostly east of the Jordan. The freed man tells his story here (5:20).

books.name: Derbe
books.line: Paul and Barnabas make many disciples here (14:20-21). Its site is not certain: it is drawn at Kerti Höyük, the usual choice, and Devri Şehri, a few kilometres away, has also been proposed.

books.name: Derbe
books.line: The farthest town of Paul's first trip in the south of the province (Acts 14:20-21). Its exact site is not certain.

books.name: Dothan
books.line: In the hills north of Shechem. Joseph finds his brothers here with the flocks, and they throw him into a pit and sell him (37:17-28).

books.name: Dothan
books.line: Where the Arameans surrounded Elisha, and his servant saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire (6:13-17).

books.name: Emmaus
books.line: Where two disciples know the risen Jesus at supper (24:13-35). Its site is uncertain: Nicopolis, Abu Ghosh, El-Qubeibeh and Motza are all proposed. Placed roughly.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: Paul teaches here about two years, so that all who live in Asia hear the word (19:10). The silversmiths of Artemis start a riot that fills the theatre (19:23-41).

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: Where Paul wrote, planning to stay “until Pentecost” because a great door for work had opened (16:8-9). Aquila and Prisca send greetings from here (16:19).

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The chief city of the province of Asia, where Paul had worked for more than two years. He tells of hardships in Asia so heavy that he despaired of life (1:8). The letter does not say where in Asia.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The leading city of the province of Asia, with its great temple of Artemis, where Paul taught for more than two years (Acts 19). The letter bears its name, though some early copies leave it out (1:1).

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: Some think Paul wrote from a prison here in the mid-50s, much closer to Philippi than Rome (1:13).

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The leading city of Asia, where Paul taught two years (Acts 19:10). Some think he wrote from a prison here.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The leading city of Asia, with its great temple of Artemis. Paul left Timothy here to correct the church's own teachers (1:3).

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The leading city of Asia, where Onesiphorus had served Paul (1:18) and where Paul sent Tychicus (4:12). Timothy seems to be here or nearby.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The leading city of Asia, about 120 miles from Colossae. Many think Paul wrote from a prison here.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The letter names no place. Early tradition places John's last years here, in the Roman province of Asia, and most readers think the churches that saw the split of 2:19 were in this region.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The letter names no place. Early tradition places John's last years here, in the Roman province of Asia, and the church has long linked these letters with John there.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The letter names no place. Early tradition places John's last years here, in the Roman province of Asia, and the church has long linked the letters of John with him there.

books.name: Ephesus
books.line: The first church addressed, in the greatest city of the province of Asia, famous for its temple of Artemis. Doctrinally careful, it had left its first love (2:1-7).

books.name: Galatia
books.line: The inland province where Paul had founded churches (Acts 14; 16:6). Placed roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The hill country east of the Jordan. Laban catches up with Jacob here, and they set up a heap of stones as a witness between them (31:21-55).

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The hill country east of the Jordan. The tribes of Reuben and Gad saw that it was good for livestock and asked to settle there (32:1). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The hill country east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon and Og and given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (3:12-13). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan to which Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh went home (22:9). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan: Jair's towns, Jephthah's home, and Jabesh-gilead (10:3-4; 11:1; 21:8). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan. Saul's first victory saved Jabesh-gilead (chapter 11), and its men buried him at the end (31:11-13). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan. Abner made Ish-bosheth king over it (2:9), and Absalom's army camped there (17:26). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan. Elijah came from here (17:1), and Ahab died fighting for Ramoth-gilead (22:3). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan. Jehu was anointed at Ramoth-gilead (9:1-6), Hazael took it (10:32-33), and Assyria carried off its people (15:29). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The land east of the Jordan, home of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (5:9-16). The men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul (10:11-12). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Gilead
books.line: The hill country east of the Jordan, placed roughly. ‘Gilead is Mine’, God says (60:7).

books.name: Goshen
books.line: Abraham goes down to Egypt in a famine (12:10). Later Jacob's family settles in Goshen, in Egypt, when Joseph brings them there (45:10; 47:27). Goshen is usually placed in the eastern Nile delta; it is drawn here roughly.

books.name: Goshen
books.line: Where Jacob's family settled and Israel lived in Egypt, spared the flies and the hail (8:22; 9:26). Goshen is usually placed in the eastern Nile delta; it is drawn here roughly.

books.name: Goshen, in Egypt
books.line: Leviticus looks back to ‘the land of Egypt, where you used to live’ (18:3). Israel had lived in Goshen, usually placed in the eastern Nile delta; it is drawn here roughly.

books.name: Haran
books.line: Terah's family settles here on the way to Canaan, and Abraham leaves from here at seventy-five (11:31 to 12:4). Jacob later flees here to his uncle Laban and works for him twenty years (chapters 29 to 31).

books.name: Hebron (Mamre)
books.line: Abraham settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron (13:18), where three visitors come to him (chapter 18). He buys a cave here to bury Sarah (chapter 23). Mamre is usually placed just north of the town.

books.name: Hebron
books.line: The scouts ‘went up through the Negev and came to Hebron’ (13:22), where Abraham had lived. They saw strong people there and lost heart.

books.name: Hebron
books.line: The town given to Caleb (14:13), and one of the six cities of refuge (20:7).

books.name: Hebron
books.line: Taken by Judah and given to Caleb (1:10, 1:20). Samson carried the gates of Gaza to a hill facing it (16:3).

books.name: Hebron
books.line: Among the towns of Judah to which David sent a share of the plunder taken back from the Amalekites (30:26-31).

books.name: Hebron
books.line: The men of Judah anointed David king here (2:4), and later all the elders of Israel (5:3). Absalom began his revolt here (15:10).

books.name: Hebron
books.line: All Israel came to David here and anointed him king (11:1-3; 12:23-38). He had reigned here seven years (29:27).

books.name: Hebron
books.line: One of the fortified cities Rehoboam built up in Judah (11:5-10).

books.name: Hebron
books.line: Called by its old name, Kiriath-arba. Some of the people of Judah lived there and in its villages (11:25).

books.name: Hierapolis
books.line: The third city of the valley, where Epaphras also laboured for the believers (4:13).

books.name: Iconium
books.line: Many Jews and Greeks believe here, but the city is divided. When a plot is made to stone them, Paul and Barnabas flee (14:1-6).

books.name: Iconium
books.line: Today's Konya, in the south of the province. Paul and Barnabas started a church here (Acts 14:1-7). On the south Galatian view, one of the churches this letter went to.

books.name: Iconium
books.line: Where there was a plot to stone Paul and Barnabas (Acts 14:5; 2 Timothy 3:11).

books.name: Italy
books.line: ‘Those from Italy send you greetings’ (13:24). It may mean people in Italy, or Italians living elsewhere greeting friends at home. The letter does not say where it was written from or to. Placed roughly.

books.name: Jericho
books.line: The book ends with Israel camped ‘in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho’ (22:1). The plains lay east of the river; the town is across it, in Canaan.

books.name: Jericho
books.line: Moses spoke on the plains of Moab, east of the river. Mount Nebo, where he died, is ‘in the land of Moab across from Jericho’ (32:49). The town itself is in Canaan.

books.name: Jericho
books.line: The first city Israel came to after crossing the river. Rahab lived here, and here the wall fell (chapters 2 and 6).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: The City of Palms, Jericho or its oasis, which Eglon of Moab took and held for eighteen years (3:13-14).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: David's envoys, shamed by the Ammonite king, waited here until their beards grew back (10:5).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: In Ahab's days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt it, at the cost of two of his sons, as Joshua had said (16:34).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: Elisha healed its spring (2:19-22). Zedekiah was overtaken in its plains as he fled (25:5).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: ‘The City of Palms’, where the men of Ephraim brought back the captives from Judah (28:15).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: Its men are on the list of returnees, 345 of them (2:34).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: ‘The men of Jericho built next to Eliashib’ the high priest, near the Sheep Gate (3:2).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: On the road up to Jerusalem, two blind men call Jesus ‘Son of David’ and are healed (20:29-34).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: The last town on the road up to Jerusalem. Blind Bartimaeus is healed here (10:46-52).

books.name: Jericho
books.line: An oasis town near the Jordan, the last stop before the climb to Jerusalem. A blind man is healed and Zacchaeus climbs a tree here (19:1-10).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Its king led the five kings of the south against Gibeon (10:1-5). Judah could not drive out its people (15:63).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Called Jebus, and still held by the Jebusites (1:21). The Levite would not stay the night there among foreigners (19:10-12).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: David brought Goliath's head to Jerusalem (17:54). The city was taken from the Jebusites only later, in David's reign (2 Samuel 5:6-7).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The Jebusite fortress of Zion, taken by David and named the City of David (5:6-9). The ark came here (6:17), and David fled the city before Absalom (15:14).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: David's city, where Solomon built the house of the LORD (6:1) and brought up the ark (8:1-6). Shishak plundered its treasures (14:25-26).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: David's city. Sennacherib's officers mocked Hezekiah outside its wall (18:17-35), the LORD defended it (19:34), and Babylon burned it (25:8-10).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The Jebusite fortress of Zion, taken by David (11:4-7). The ark came here (15:3), and Ornan's threshing floor became the site of the temple (22:1).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Solomon built the temple on Mount Moriah (3:1), the place God chose (7:12). Babylon burned it (36:19).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The city of the house of God. The returnees rebuilt the altar here (3:1-3) and finished the temple (6:15), and Ezra arrived in the fifth month (7:8).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The city whose wall Nehemiah rebuilt in fifty-two days (6:15) and dedicated with two choirs singing on top of it (12:27-43).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Mordecai's family was carried into exile from here with King Jeconiah (2:6). The whole story of Esther takes place far to the east, in Susa.

books.name: Jerusalem (Zion)
books.line: The city on its hill, where the temple stood. ‘I have installed My King on Zion’ (2:6). The exiles in Babylon wept when they remembered it (137:1).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The city the whole book mourns, ‘once so full of people’ (1:1). Mount Zion, its temple hill, lies desolate (5:18).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Herod's city and the temple's. It is troubled at the news of a new king (2:3), welcomes Jesus as Son of David (21:9), and he dies outside it.

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The city of the temple. Opponents come down from it early (3:22). Jesus walks toward it from 8:27, and dies outside it.

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The city of the temple, where the book begins and ends. Jesus sets his face toward it (9:51), weeps over it, dies outside its walls and rises.

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The city of the temple and the feasts. Pools uncovered by archaeologists are widely taken to be Bethesda (5:2) and Siloam (9:7). Jesus dies outside its walls.

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line:
Where the book begins. The Spirit comes here at Pentecost, the first believers meet in the temple courts, and Stephen is stoned outside the city (7:58).

Paul and Barnabas bring the question of the Gentiles to the apostles and elders here (15:2). Years later Paul is seized in the temple and arrested (21:27-33).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Where Paul was about to take the gift from Macedonia and Achaia for the poor believers (15:25-26). He asks the Romans to pray for his safety there (15:31).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Where the collection for the poor believers was to go. Corinth's own messengers would carry the gift (16:3).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Where the poor believers lived for whom Paul gathered the collection of chapters 8 and 9. Romans names the city: the gift was “for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem” (Romans 15:26).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Where Paul stayed fifteen days with Peter (1:18), and where, fourteen years later, the leaders gave him “the right hand of fellowship” (2:9).

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: Where the temple stood. Paul says the lawless one will seat himself ‘in the temple of God’ (2:4); readers differ on whether he meant this temple or spoke in a figure.

books.name: Jerusalem
books.line: The letter names no place. The church has long named James the brother of Jesus as the writer, and he led the church here (Acts 15:13; Galatians 2:9). If he wrote it, he most likely wrote from here.

books.name: Joppa
books.line: The port, today's Jaffa. Cedar logs from Lebanon were brought here by sea for the temple (3:7).

books.name: Joppa
books.line: An old port, today's Jaffa. Peter raises Tabitha here, and on a rooftop here he sees the vision that sends him to Cornelius (9:36 to 10:16).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: The river between the camp and the land. The last laws of the book begin, ‘When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan’ (35:10).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: The river Moses was not allowed to cross: ‘See the land with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan’ (3:27).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: Israel crossed ‘on dry ground’ opposite Jericho, with the river in flood (3:15-17).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: At its fords Ehud's men cut off Moab (3:28), and the men of Gilead stopped the Ephraimites with the word Shibboleth (12:5-6).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: When the Philistines gathered at Michmash, some Hebrews fled across the Jordan (13:7). After Gilboa, Israelites on the other side of the Jordan left their towns (31:7).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: David crossed it fleeing from Absalom (17:22), and came back across it as king (19:15-18).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: The temple's bronze was cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan (7:46). Elijah hid by a brook east of it (17:3).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: Elijah and then Elisha parted it with the cloak (2:8, 14), and Naaman washed in it seven times (5:14).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: Gadite commanders crossed it in flood to join David (12:15), and David crossed it to fight the Arameans (19:17).

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: Named once, in God's word about Behemoth: ‘he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth’ (40:23). It may stand for any mighty, surging river.

books.name: The Jordan
books.line: The river of the land. A homesick singer remembers God ‘from the land of Jordan’ (42:6); at the exodus ‘the Jordan turned back’ (114:3).

books.name: The Jordan River
books.line: In the wilderness of Judea, John baptizes in the Jordan. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized (3:13-17).

books.name: The Jordan River
books.line: John baptizes here, and Jesus is baptized (1:9). Mark does not name the exact spot.

books.name: Laodicea
books.line: A city of the Lycus valley, east of Ephesus. Marcion knew this letter as ‘To the Laodiceans’, and some link it with the letter ‘from Laodicea’ of Colossians 4:16.

books.name: Laodicea
books.line: The larger city nearby. Paul asks that this letter be read there, and the letter from Laodicea in Colossae (4:16).

books.name: Laodicea
books.line: The last church addressed, in a wealthy city of the Lycus valley, known for banking, black wool and medicine. Christ calls it lukewarm, and knocks at its door (3:14-22).

books.name: Lod
books.line: The town later called Lydda. ‘The men of Lod, Hadid, and Ono’ numbered 725 (2:33).

books.name: Lod
books.line: The town later called Lydda. Its people were among the first to come home (7:37), and Benjamin's people lived there (11:35). The plain of Ono, where Nehemiah's enemies tried to lure him (6:2), lay nearby.

books.name: Lydda
books.line: A town inland from Joppa, today's Lod. Peter heals Aeneas here (9:32-35).

books.name: Lystra
books.line: Paul heals a man lame from birth, and the crowd takes him and Barnabas for gods; then Paul is stoned and left for dead (14:8-19). Timothy comes from here (16:1).

books.name: Lystra
books.line: Where Paul was stoned and left for dead (Acts 14:19). If the letter went to the south, the Galatians may have seen the scars he calls “the marks of Jesus” (6:17).

books.name: Lystra
books.line: Timothy's home town, where Paul met him, the son of a Jewish believing mother and a Greek father (Acts 16:1).

books.name: Lystra
books.line: Timothy's home town, where Paul was stoned and left for dead (Acts 14:19; 2 Timothy 3:11).

books.name: Malta
books.line: The ship runs aground and breaks up, and everyone reaches land safely (27:41 to 28:1). Where it struck is not known for sure: it is drawn at St Paul's Bay, where tradition places it.

books.name: Miletus
books.line: A port south of Ephesus. Paul sends for the elders of the church at Ephesus and says goodbye to them here (20:15-38).

books.name: Miletus
books.line: A port south of Ephesus, where Paul left Trophimus sick (4:20).

books.name: Moriah
books.line: ‘The land of Moriah’, where Abraham is sent to offer Isaac (22:2). Where exactly is uncertain. 2 Chronicles 3:1 names Mount Moriah as the site of Solomon's temple in Jerusalem, so it is drawn there, roughly.

books.name: Nain
books.line: A village on the slope of the hill of Moreh, a few miles from Nazareth. Jesus raises a widow's only son (7:11-17).

books.name: Nazareth
books.line: The small Galilee town where Jesus grows up, so that he is called a Nazarene (2:23). Later its people take offence at him (13:57).

books.name: Nazareth
books.line: Jesus' home town in Galilee, where he is not welcomed (6:1-6).

books.name: Nazareth
books.line: A small village in the hills of Galilee. Gabriel comes to Mary here; Jesus grows up here and is nearly thrown off its hill (4:29).

books.name: Nicopolis
books.line: A city on the west coast of Greece, founded by Augustus after Actium. Paul planned to winter here and asked Titus to come (3:12). Most scholars think this is the Nicopolis he meant.

books.name: Paddan-aram
books.line: The country around Haran. Rebekah's family lives here, and Jacob is sent here to find a wife (25:20; 28:2). Drawn roughly, near Haran.

books.name: Paphos
books.line: At the west end of Cyprus. The governor, Sergius Paulus, believes here after the magician Elymas is struck blind, and from here on Saul is called Paul (13:6-12).

books.name: Peniel
books.line: By the ford of the Jabbok, a river that runs down into the Jordan from the east, Jacob wrestles until dawn. He calls the place Peniel, ‘face of God’ (32:22-31). The exact spot is uncertain.

books.name: Perga
books.line: A city of Pamphylia, near the south coast. John Mark leaves the others here and goes back to Jerusalem (13:13). On the way home, Paul and Barnabas preach here (14:25).

books.name: Philippi
books.line: A Roman colony, the first city in Macedonia where Paul preaches (16:12). Lydia believes here, and Paul and Silas are beaten and thrown into prison (16:14-24).

books.name: Philippi
books.line: The leading city of its district of Macedonia (Acts 16:12), where Paul had started a church. Paul wrote this letter somewhere in Macedonia after Titus met him there (7:5-7). Philippi is often suggested, but the letter does not name the city.

books.name: Philippi
books.line: A Roman colony in Macedonia, where the church began with Lydia, a slave girl and a jailer (Acts 16). The letter is written to the saints here (1:1).

books.name: Philippi
books.line: Where Paul and Silas were beaten and jailed before they came to Thessalonica (2:2; Acts 16).

books.name: Philippi
books.line: A city of Macedonia. Paul says he went on to Macedonia (1:3); the letter does not say where in it he was.

books.name: Pisidian Antioch
books.line: Paul preaches in the synagogue here (13:16-41). When many oppose them, he and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles, and are driven out of the region (13:46-50).

books.name: Pisidian Antioch
books.line: A Roman colony in the south of the province, where Paul preached in the synagogue (Acts 13:14-52). On the south Galatian view, one of the churches this letter went to.

books.name: Pisidian Antioch
books.line: Where Paul and Barnabas were driven out of the district (Acts 13:50; 2 Timothy 3:11).

books.name: The plain of the Jordan
books.line: Lot chooses this well-watered plain and settles near Sodom (13:10-12). Where Sodom stood is not known: some place it south of the Dead Sea; others north of it.

books.name: Pontus
books.line: A province along the Black Sea coast. People from Pontus heard Peter at Pentecost (Acts 2:9). How the gospel reached it is not known. Placed roughly.

books.name: Puteoli
books.line: A port on the Bay of Naples. Paul lands here, finds believers, and stays with them a week (28:13-14).

books.name: Region of the Gadarenes
books.line: Across the lake, two men held by demons meet Jesus, and the pigs rush into the sea (8:28-34). Placed roughly.

books.name: Region of the Gerasenes
books.line: Non-Jewish country across the lake, where Jesus frees a man from a legion of spirits (5:1-20). Placed here roughly.

books.name: Rome
books.line: Where the book ends. Paul lives two years under guard in a rented house, welcoming all who come and proclaiming the kingdom of God (28:16; 28:30-31).

books.name: Rome
books.line: The capital of the empire, where the letter went: to house churches Paul had not founded and had never visited (1:13), meeting in homes (16:5).

books.name: Rome
books.line: Where Paul lived under guard for two years (Acts 28:30). Most who hold that Paul wrote the letter think he wrote it here, as ‘the prisoner of Christ Jesus’ (3:1).

books.name: Rome
books.line: Where Paul lived under guard two years (Acts 28:30). Most think he wrote here, with greetings from ‘the household of Caesar’ (4:22).

books.name: Rome
books.line: Where Paul lived under guard two years (Acts 28:30). Most who hold that Paul wrote the letter think he wrote here, in chains (4:18).

books.name: Rome
books.line: Where Paul writes, a prisoner in chains. Onesiphorus searched the city until he found him (1:17).

books.name: Rome
books.line: Where Paul lived under guard two years (Acts 28:30). The traditional view is that he wrote from here, ‘a prisoner of Christ Jesus’ (verse 1).

books.name: Rome
books.line: Most readers take ‘Babylon’ (5:13) as a name for Rome, where early tradition places Peter at the end of his life. A few take it as Babylon in Mesopotamia or in Egypt.

books.name: Salamis
books.line: A port on the east coast of Cyprus. Barnabas and Saul land here and preach in the Jewish synagogues (13:5).

books.name: Samaria
books.line: The hill country of the north, named after the capital Omri built on a hill he bought (16:24), where Ahab reigned (16:29). The book also uses the name for the region (13:32). Drawn roughly; the city is not marked.

books.name: Samaria
books.line: The northern hill country, named after Israel's capital, which Aram besieged (6:24) and Assyria took after three years (17:5-6). The book also uses the name for the region (17:24). Drawn roughly; the city is not marked.

books.name: Samaria
books.line: The northern capital. Jehoshaphat visited Ahab there (18:2), and the prophet Oded met the army bringing captives (28:9). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Samaria
books.line: The province to the north. Peoples the Assyrians had settled ‘in the cities of Samaria’ opposed the rebuilding (4:10), and the king's reply went to his officials there (4:17). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Samaria
books.line: The province to the north, governed by Sanballat. He mocked the builders before ‘the army of Samaria’ (4:2). Drawn roughly.

books.name: Samaria
books.line: The region between Galilee and Judea, whose people most Jews kept apart from. Philip preaches the Christ in a city there (8:5).

books.name: Samaritan villages
books.line: The land between Galilee and Judea. A Samaritan village refuses Jesus (9:52); a Samaritan leper comes back to thank him (17:16). Placed roughly.

books.name: Shechem
books.line: Abraham's first stop in Canaan, where God promises the land and Abraham builds an altar (12:6-7). Jacob later camps here, and Dinah is attacked here (chapter 34).

books.name: Shechem
books.line: Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal stand on either side of the valley at Shechem. There the tribes were to stand for the blessing and the curse (11:29; 27:12-13).

books.name: Shechem
books.line: Between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. Here the law was read (8:30-35) and the covenant renewed (24:1), and here Joseph was buried (24:32).

books.name: Shechem
books.line: Abimelech's mother's town, whose leaders made him king and whom he later destroyed (chapter 9).

books.name: Shechem
books.line: All Israel gathered here to make Rehoboam king, and the north broke away (12:1-20). Jeroboam built it up (12:25).

books.name: Shechem
books.line: An old city in the hill country. In Psalm 60 God claims his land town by town, beginning with Shechem.

books.name: Sidon
books.line: Joab's census went north as far as Sidon (24:6).

books.name: Sidon
books.line: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians (16:31). Elijah was sent to a widow at Zarephath of Sidon (17:9).

books.name: Sidon
books.line: The other port city of Phoenicia. Its people, with those of Tyre, shipped the cedar (3:7).

books.name: Sidon
books.line: A Gentile port to the north. Jesus says it would have turned to God if it had seen what Galilee saw (11:21-22).

books.name: Sidon
books.line: A port north of Tyre. People come from here to hear Jesus (3:8).

books.name: Sidon
books.line: A port city on the coast north of Galilee. With Tyre, it asks Herod Agrippa for peace because it depends on his land for food (12:20).

books.name: Sodom
books.line: The city Lot settles near (13:12), destroyed in chapter 19. Where it stood is not known. It is drawn at the south end of the Dead Sea, one of the places proposed, roughly.

books.name: Sodom
books.line: The city overthrown in an instant (4:6). Where it stood is not known. It is drawn roughly at the south end of the Dead Sea, one of the places proposed, as on the Genesis map.

books.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
books.line: The cities God condemned in Lot's day, ‘reducing them to ashes’ (2:6; Genesis 19). Where they stood is not known. Drawn at the south end of the Dead Sea, one of the places proposed, roughly.

books.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
books.line: The cities Jude gives as ‘an example’ of judgment (1:7; Genesis 19). Where they stood is not known. Drawn at the south end of the Dead Sea, one of the places proposed, roughly.

books.name: Sychar
books.line: A Samaritan town near Jacob's well, where Jesus talks with the woman at noon (4:5-42). Most place it at the village of Askar; some at old Shechem.

books.name: Syracuse
books.line: A great city of Sicily. Paul's ship stops here three days on the way to Italy (28:12).

books.name: Tarsus
books.line: Paul's home city in Cilicia (21:39). After his first visit to Jerusalem the believers send him here, and Barnabas later comes to bring him to Antioch (9:30; 11:25-26).

books.name: Tarsus
books.line: Paul's home town, in Cilicia. After his first visit to Jerusalem he went to “the regions of Syria and Cilicia” (1:21).

books.name: Thessalonica
books.line: Paul reasons from the Scriptures in the synagogue for three Sabbaths (17:1-3). A mob attacks Jason's house, and the believers send Paul away by night (17:5-10).

books.name: Thessalonica
books.line: Where the Philippians sent Paul help more than once, soon after he left them (4:16).

books.name: Thessalonica
books.line: Capital of Macedonia, a port on the great Roman road. The church Paul founded here had to watch him leave by night (1:1; Acts 17:1-10).

books.name: Thessalonica
books.line: The church the letter was written to, still suffering for its faith and frightened by talk of the end (1:1, 4; 2:2).

books.name: Thessalonica
books.line: The capital of Macedonia, where Paul had founded a church years before (Acts 17). The letter does not say whether he was here.

books.name: Thessalonica
books.line: Where Demas went when he left Paul, ‘in his love of this world’ (4:10).

books.name: Tiberias
books.line: A new city built by Herod Antipas and named for the emperor. John calls the lake the Sea of Tiberias, where the risen Jesus meets his disciples (21:1).

books.name: Troas
books.line: A port near old Troy. Here Paul sees in the night a man of Macedonia asking for help (16:8-10). Years later Eutychus falls from a window here during Paul's long talk (20:6-12).

books.name: Troas
books.line: A port on the coast of Asia Minor. A door stood open for the gospel here, but Paul had no peace without Titus, and crossed over to Macedonia (2:12-13).

books.name: Troas
books.line: A port where Paul left his cloak with Carpus, and his scrolls (4:13).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedar, carpenters and stonemasons to build David's palace (5:11). The census reached the fortress of Tyre (24:7).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen for the temple (5:1-10), and Huram the bronze-worker came from here (7:13-14).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen for David's palace (14:1), and the people of Tyre brought cedar for the temple (22:4).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: Solomon asked Hiram king of Tyre for cedar, as he had sent to David (2:3).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: With Sidon, its people were paid in food, drink and oil to bring cedar from Lebanon for the temple (3:7).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: The Phoenician trading city. Its men sold fish and goods in Jerusalem on the Sabbath (13:16).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: A rich port city to the north. In Psalm 87 even Tyre is counted among those born in Zion.

books.name: Tyre
books.line: A Gentile city on the coast. In its district a Canaanite mother's great faith is praised (15:21-28).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: A non-Jewish port city on the coast. Jesus meets a Syrophoenician woman in its region (7:24-30).

books.name: Tyre
books.line: The other great port of Phoenicia, south of Sidon. Its people come to Herod Agrippa at Caesarea to ask for peace (12:20).

books.name: Ur
books.line: Abraham's family sets out from ‘Ur of the Chaldeans’ (11:28-31). Ur is usually placed at Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Mesopotamia, where it is drawn here; some have proposed a northern Ur near Haran instead.
